name: μ-centred slerp
plain: Slerp around a population centroid rather than the origin. It subtracts μ, slerps directions, lerps the radius, adds μ back. Useful when the latent has a non-zero mean, because origin-centred slerp then bends through a different arc. When μ is not given, the function uses per-channel mean over batch and space.
math:
ã=a−μ, b̃=b−μ, ω=acos(clamp(â·b̂))
out=μ+[sin((1−t)ω)/sin ω·â+sin(tω)/sin ω·b̂]·((1−t)‖ã‖+t‖b̃‖)
sin ω<1e−4 → lerp. Variance kept via radius lerp around μ.
